name: Bawang
commonUses: Traditionally used in the Philippines as support for high cholesterol and mild blood pressure management.
warnings: May increase bleeding risk when combined with blood thinners. Consult a doctor before using with maintenance medicines.
estimatedPrice: Price varies by preparation and pharmacy

name: Sambong
commonUses: Used in Philippine herbal practice as a diuretic and as supportive care for kidney stones and uric acid concerns.
warnings: Use with caution in dehydration or kidney problems. Increase water intake and consult a clinician for persistent symptoms.
estimatedPrice: Price varies by preparation and pharmacy

name: Tsaang-gubat
commonUses: Traditionally used for mild stomach pain and diarrhea support.
warnings: Not a substitute for treatment of severe abdominal pain, bloody stool, or dehydration.
estimatedPrice: Price varies by preparation and pharmacy

name: Ampalaya
commonUses: Used in Philippine herbal practice as support for blood sugar control.
warnings: May lower blood sugar. Use carefully with diabetes medicines to avoid hypoglycemia.
estimatedPrice: Price varies by preparation and pharmacy

name: Yerba Buena
commonUses: Traditionally used for mild body pain, headache, and toothache relief.
warnings: Seek proper dental or medical care if pain persists or worsens.
estimatedPrice: Price varies by preparation and pharmacy

name: Ulasimang Bato
commonUses: Used in Philippine herbal practice to help manage uric acid and gout-related symptoms.
warnings: Consult a doctor for severe joint swelling, fever, or kidney disease. Do not rely on herbal therapy alone for acute gout attacks.
estimatedPrice: Price varies by preparation and pharmacy

name: Bayabas
commonUses: Traditionally used for wound washing, mouth rinse for swollen gums, and mild diarrhea support.
warnings: External or supportive use does not replace antibiotics or proper wound care for infected wounds.
estimatedPrice: Price varies by preparation and pharmacy

name: Akapulko
commonUses: Traditionally used for fungal skin infections such as ringworm, an-an, and athlete's foot.
warnings: For external use only unless specifically advised. Stop use if skin irritation becomes severe.
estimatedPrice: Price varies by preparation and pharmacy

name: Lagundi
commonUses: Used in the Philippines as supportive treatment for cough and mild respiratory symptoms.
warnings: Seek medical care for difficulty breathing, prolonged fever, chest pain, or worsening cough.
estimatedPrice: Price varies by preparation and pharmacy

name: Niyog-niyogan
commonUses: Traditionally used in the Philippines for intestinal worms.
warnings: Too much may cause stomach pain, nausea, or diarrhea. Follow age-appropriate dosing guidance.
